items.title: 14.3 Cross Product or Vector Product (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Assalam o alaikum! Ab hum Unit 14 ke teesre hisse mein aa gaye hain. Kitab mein heading 14.3 Cross Product or Vector Product ke foran baad pehli sub-heading 14.3.1 shuru ho jati hai; main heading ke neeche alag se kuch nahin likha. Is liye yeh safha hamari taraf se is poore hisse ka naqsha (overview) hai, taa ke aap ko pehle se pata ho ke aage kya aa raha hai aur kis cheez ki tayyari kar ke aana hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Pichle hisse 14.2 mein humne do vectors ko dot product se multiply kiya tha aur jawab ek scalar (sirf ek number, jis ki koi direction nahin) aaya tha. Ab 14.3 mein do vectors ko multiply karne ka doosra tareeqa seekhenge: cross product \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v}\).
Is ka jawab ek vector hota hai, yani number ke saath saath ek direction bhi. Aur yeh vector \(\underline{u}\) aur \(\underline{v}\) dono par perpendicular (amood, 90 degree par khara) hota hai. Isi liye ise vector product bhi kehte hain.
Cross product sirf space (teen dimensions) wale vectors ke liye define hai. Kyun? Socho: agar do vectors ek kaghaz (plane) par pare hon to un dono par perpendicular direction kaghaz se bahar nikalti hai, yani teesri dimension chahiye. Flat kaghaz ki duniya (2D) mein aisi direction hoti hi nahin.

rows: Tarteeb se sign badal jata hai: \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v} = -(\underline{v} \times \underline{u})\)
Perpendicular vectors ka dot product zero
Parallel vectors ka cross product zero vector
Angle, projection, work done mein kaam aata hai
Perpendicular vector, area, moment of force mein kaam aata hai
blocks.caption: Dot product aur cross product ka muqabla (hamari taraf se)

blocks.text: Aage aane wali sub-headings ek nazar mein, taa ke aap ko raasta maloom rahe:

items: 14.3.1 Definition \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v} = (|\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\sin\theta)\,\underline{n}\) aur direction maloom karne ka right hand rule (seedhe haath ka qaida).
14.3.2 Parallel vectors: in ka cross product \(\underline{0}\) (zero vector) hota hai.
14.3.3 \(\underline{i}, \underline{j}, \underline{k}\) ke aapas ke cross products, aur yeh nateeja ke \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v} = -\underline{v} \times \underline{u}\).
14.3.5 Components se \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v}\) nikalne ka determinant formula (Example 15). Yeh sab se zyada istemal hone wala formula hai.
14.3.6 Do vectors ke darmiyan angle ka sine (Examples 16-19), jin mein trigonometry ke mashhoor formulas bhi saabit honge.
14.3.7 Asal zindagi mein istemal: parallelogram aur triangle ka area, aur force ka moment (Examples 20-22).

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text:
Shuru karne se pehle do cheezein dohra lijiye, kyun ke yeh poore hisse mein baar baar aayengi:
1. Unit vectors \(\underline{i}, \underline{j}, \underline{k}\) jo \(x\), \(y\) aur \(z\) axes ki taraf hain, aur magnitude (lambai) ka formula \(|a\underline{i} + b\underline{j} + c\underline{k}| = \sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}}\).
2. \(3 \times 3\) determinant ko pehli row ke saath kholna: \(\begin{vmatrix} p & q & r \\ a & b & c \\ d & e & f \end{vmatrix} = p(bf - ce) - q(af - cd) + r(ae - bd)\). Dhyan dein: beech wale term par minus ka sign hota hai. Yahi minus aage cross product mein \(\underline{j}\) wale hisse par aayega.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Determinant kholne ki practice (yeh hamari misaal hai, kitab ka sawal nahin): \(\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 2 & 0 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\).
Pehla term: \(1(1 \cdot 1 - 4 \cdot 0) = 1\). Doosra term: \(-2(0 \cdot 1 - 4 \cdot 2) = -2(-8) = 16\). Teesra term: \(3(0 \cdot 0 - 1 \cdot 2) = -6\).
Jawab: \(1 + 16 - 6 = 11\). Agar yeh aasani se ho gaya to aap 14.3.5 ke liye tayyar hain.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar \(\underline{u}\) aur \(\underline{v}\) dono \(xy\)-plane (farsh) mein pare hon, to \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v}\) kis axis ki seedh mein hoga? (Jawab: \(z\)-axis ki seedh mein, upar ya neeche, kyun ke wahi direction farsh par perpendicular hai.)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Do vectors ka cross product ek vector hai; dot product ek scalar.
2. \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v}\) hamesha \(\underline{u}\) aur \(\underline{v}\) dono par perpendicular hota hai.
3. Cross product sirf space (3D) ke vectors ke liye define hai.
4. Determinant kholte waqt beech wale term par minus yaad rakhiye.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(\times\) ko aam numbers wali zarb samajhna: vectors ki tarteeb badalne se jawab ka sign badal jata hai. \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v}\) aur \(\underline{v} \times \underline{u}\) barabar nahin, ek doosre ke ulte hain.
2. Cross product ka jawab number likh dena. \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v}\) vector hai; sirf us ki magnitude \(|\underline{u} \times \underline{v}|\) number hoti hai.
3. Dot \(\cdot\) aur cross \(\times\) ka nishan aapas mein mila dena. Sawal parhte waqt nishan ghaur se dekhiye.
